gaps.sentence: Students ___ leave the examination room without permission.
gaps.explanation: Formal rules use 'may not' (or 'must not') to deny permission: may not leave.

gaps.sentence: When I was a child, I ___ stay up late on New Year's Eve.
gaps.hint: permission that existed in the past
gaps.explanation: 'Was allowed to' expresses past permission; 'could' is also possible: was allowed to.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ leave any bags unattended; security removes them at once.
gaps.explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition; 'need not' would mean it is optional.

gaps.sentence: It ___ be the postman — he has already been this morning.
gaps.hint: ruled out by what already happened
gaps.explanation: Evidence that rules something out uses 'can't': can't be.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather stay in tonight, if that's all right.
We ___ have hurried — the concert was cancelled anyway.
gaps.hint: the rush turned out to be unnecessary
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have hurried' means we hurried although it was unnecessary: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: In this lab, food and drink ___ be brought past the reception area.
gaps.explanation: Written prohibitions use 'must not': must not be brought.

gaps.sentence: ___ you swim when you were four years old?
gaps.explanation: 'Could' asks about past ability: Could you swim.
